items.title: Tom Malone interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 3, 2023
items.q: So people like Alan Rubin, Marvin Stamm, Lou Marini, George Young, the Brecker brothers — we would book stuff

ctx.x: Indeed. He told me that some — he didn’t mention names — but he said when the studio scene was so happening that guys would get a little over-zealous and take — if they had a ten to one and then they would book a one to four, knowing that either they were going to have to get out of something early or arrive late.

Well we did that frequently during the 70s and 80s. You know I basically played Saturday Night Live on the weekend and I did recording sessions all during the week. And I was in a group of people who were in demand. So people like Alan Rubin, Marvin Stamm, Lou Marini, George Young, the Brecker brothers — we would book stuff — we’d book a jingle from one to two and another jingle two to three. And we would usually get it done early because we knew we had another session. And that’s why they booked us, they knew…

in walking distance. So if we showed up ten minutes late we all showed up together and we got the job done. So even though that happened occasionally — I got into the business in New York — I met Bill Watrous early on and he would send me in to sub for him, to cover. I’d show up and I’d say, “Bill Watrous will be here in ten minutes,” and I’d play until he got there. And that’s the way I established myself in the business. Yeah. Bill Watrous and I became friends.
